grammar.title: Possessing formally with 具有
grammar.pattern: (主语) + 具有 + 抽象名词
grammar.explanation: 具有 (jùyǒu) is a formal way to say "to possess, to have" — used with abstract qualities or characteristics rather than physical objects. It's common in written or professional Chinese.

grammar.title: Whatever you do... with 千万
grammar.pattern: 千万 + 不要/别 + 动词短语
grammar.explanation: 千万 (qiānwàn) adds strong emphasis to a warning or request — "whatever you do, be sure to (not)...". It's almost always paired with 不要 or 别 right before the verb.

sentences.zh: 开车的时候千万要小心。
sentences.pinyin: Kāichē de shíhou qiānwàn yào xiǎoxīn.
sentences.en: Whatever you do, be careful while driving.

sentences.zh: 这件事你千万别告诉别人。
sentences.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì nǐ qiānwàn bié gàosu biérén.
sentences.en: Whatever you do, don't tell others about this matter.

sentences.pinyin: Tiānqì bù hǎo, qiānwàn bié chūmén.
sentences.en: The weather's bad; whatever you do, don't go out.

sentences.zh: 这个计划具有很大的意义。
sentences.pinyin: Zhège jìhuà jùyǒu hěn dà de yìyì.
Tā jùyǒu hěn qiáng de nénglì.

sentences.zh: 这份工作具有一定的危险。
sentences.pinyin: Zhè fèn gōngzuò jùyǒu yīdìng de wēixiǎn.
sentences.en: This job has a certain amount of danger.
